articles.summary: Starting January 1, 2027, the way pregnancy care is billed to insurance changes across the country. The care does not change. The paperwork behind it does. Here is what patients are likely to notice, in plain language, plus a short script for the front desk staff who are about to start getting these questions.
articles.title: Your pregnancy bill is changing in January. Here is what it means.

articles.title: We asked an AI assistant to book a knee surgeon at 86 health systems. It couldn't book one.

articles.summary: The 2027 maternity transition has been quiet so far, and that quiet is misleading. Almost every practice is still billing the global the way it always has, so the denials have not started. Here is why January is when we find out, and what that means for your cash flow.
articles.title: No one has seen a maternity denial yet. January is the real test.

articles.summary: On 30 October, HHS published a guidance letter allowing HIPAA covered entities to use CPT 2026 maternity codes between 1 January and 31 December 2027, for pregnancies that start in 2026 and end in 2027. Read the next sentence carefully, because payers may issue business rules under it. May, not must. It does not let you keep using the old codes. It lets your payers decide whether you can.
articles.title: You can keep billing 2026 maternity codes until the end of 2027, if your payer lets you
